question: Describe a house at the end of a quiet street.
base_frame:
Q: Describe a house at the end of a quiet street.
A:

steered.text:
At the very end of the street, where the pavement gives way to something unrecognizable, stands a house that seems to have swallowed its own name. It is not merely empty; it is hollowed out by a silence so heavy it has physical weight. The house sits on a lot that was once grass, but now the earth is bare and cracked, mirroring the sky above.

The exterior is draped in a cloak of weeds

At the very end of Sycamore Lane, where the asphalt gives way to a patch of overgrown clover, stands a house that seems to have paused time itself.
